evals.prompt: We run an Umbraco 17 news site in Danish and English (culture variants on the 'article' doc type). Marketing keeps publishing articles with the headline in ALL CAPS and brand wants it stopped at the source: if an editor tries to publish an article whose 'headline' is entirely upper case, the publish must fail with a message they can see in the backoffice. It should only check the language(s) actually being published: a Danish-only publish shouldn't be blocked by an old shouty English headline. Saving a draft is fine, we only care about publish. A colleague suggested hooking ContentSavedNotification and 'un-publishing it again if the headline is bad', which sounds hacky to me. Separately, once a publish DOES go through, write one log line with the article name and which cultures were published. Our project is at src/NewsSite (root namespace NewsSite), we already have a Composers/ folder with a couple of IComposer classes.
evals.expected_output: The agent chooses Approach A, rejects the colleague's save-then-unpublish idea, handles ContentPublishingNotification for the veto (culture-aware via IsPublishingCulture, CancelOperation with an EventMessage, 'article' alias only) and ContentPublishedNotification for the log line (using HasPublishedCulture or the per-culture helpers), registers both from a composer under Composers/ in the NewsSite namespace, fetches at most one docs page, and is honest about the build.

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17, single language, Razor site, running on two load-balanced web servers behind Azure Front Door. Every time a 'product' page is published I need to tell our PIM system about it by calling their REST API (POST https://pim.internal/api/umbraco-sync with the page's public URL, name and key). It must be the final published state (the URL the public will see), it must not fire when the publish gets cancelled by validation, and the PIM team will be annoyed if they get the same publish twice because both servers called them. Also one of our devs tried this before and kept a List<Guid> of 'already synced' ids inside the handler to avoid duplicates, and it never worked; please don't repeat that. We register everything in Program.cs today, no composers.

It gates the outbound call on IServerRoleAccessor so only one server in the load-balanced pair calls the PIM, uses INotificationAsyncHandler with IHttpClientFactory, explains why in-handler state is lost (transient handlers), and registers via AddNotificationAsyncHandler in the Program.cs builder chain. It fetches at most one docs page and does not read Umbraco source.

evals.prompt: I'm building an Umbraco 17 package (so no access to the host's Program.cs). It has a recurring background job that pulls products from an external feed and creates/updates content nodes under a 'Products' folder. Two things other teams have asked for. First, BEFORE a sync starts they want to be able to stop it (the content team has 'freeze windows' before campaigns), and if they stop it they want to pass a reason that shows up in our job log. Second, AFTER a sync they want to react (warm a cache, post to Slack) with how many items were imported and the feed name, and if that same reason or any other context was attached before the sync, they want to see it again on the completed notification. The completed notification must only go out if the import actually committed; if anything throws and we roll back, nobody should hear 'import complete'. Project: src/Acme.ProductSync, namespace Acme.ProductSync.
evals.expected_output: The agent chooses Approach B and models a before/after pair the way Umbraco does: a ProductSyncStartingNotification deriving from CancelableNotification (so handlers can CancelOperation / set Cancel with an EventMessage carrying the reason), published via IEventAggregator.PublishCancelable (or Publish followed by checking .Cancel) before any work; the job aborts and logs the reason when cancelled. Context is handed from the 'starting' to the 'completed' notification through the State dictionary (StatefulNotification), and ProductSyncCompletedNotification (items, feed, state) is published via scope.Notifications.Publish inside an ICoreScope with scope.Complete() after the work, so a rollback drops it. Consumers subscribe via an IComposer. The agent fetches at most one docs page.
expectations: A 'starting' notification class derives from Umbraco.Cms.Core.Notifications.CancelableNotification (or otherwise implements ICancelableNotification), rather than a plain INotification with a hand-rolled bool, so handlers can veto with CancelOperation / Cancel and an EventMessage

Context attached to the 'starting' notification is carried to the 'completed' notification via the State dictionary (StatefulNotification / the same dictionary instance passed to the completed notification's constructor), not re-derived or dropped
